# On-chain Forensics API


## Free developer key (no card, no payment signature)

    curl -X POST https://api.onchainforensics.dev/functions/devKeys \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"email":"you@example.com"}'

Returns a key (shown once) worth 10,000 calls per calendar month on the cached verdict tier.
Send it as the X-Dev-Key header. One key per email, one per caller per day, resets on the 1st (UTC).
Above the cap, prepaid packs at /functions/forensicsCredits ($25 for 25,000 calls) use the same header
pattern. The MCP server picks the key up from FORENSICS_DEV_KEY and needs no other setup.


## Install inside your agent (no code)

    npx -y github:leohoudinisanders-byte/forensics-mcp

On-chain Forensics ships an MCP server (stdio, zero dependencies, six tools: token_verdict,
token_mints, settlesafe_check, token_profile, wallet_profile, forensics_catalog). Load it in
Claude Desktop, Cursor, Claude Code, LangChain or any MCP client. When the free allowance on a
route is spent the tool returns the decoded x402 challenge instead of an error, so you always
know the exact price before paying. Latency numbers and our deprecation policy:
https://onchainforensics.dev/status.html

> Decision-grade on-chain forensics for AI agents. Ask the question you are actually asking: should I touch this token or wallet? Pay per call in USDC on Base via x402, no API keys, no signup. Verdict returns a letter grade and a one-line roast, so a caller gets a call to make, not a dashboard to read.

## Start here (cheapest path to a decision)

1. verdict, $0.02, the core call. Ends in a letter grade A to F, risk flags and a one-line roast.
   GET /functions/forensicsApi?endpoint=verdict&address=0x<token>&chain=base|ethereum
2. settlesafe, $0.02, adds the settle question: is this token safe to accept right now, or is it paused, fee-trapped or clawback-capable.
   GET /functions/forensicsApi?endpoint=settlesafe&address=0x<token>&chain=base|ethereum
3. mints, $0.02, answers who is adding supply and how much in the window.
   GET /functions/forensicsMints?token=0x<token>&chain=base|ethereum

Three calls, $0.06, and you can decide whether to trade, settle against it, or walk away. Every verdict payload already returns the next two calls with ready-to-fire URLs, so an agent never has to guess what to buy next.

## Prepaid credit packs: pay once, then stop signing

If an agent is going to make hundreds or thousands of calls, buying credit once is cheaper in effort
than signing a payment per call:

- `POST https://solene-fa2010da.base44.app/functions/forensicsCredits?plan=pack25` at **$25.00** returns
  an `api_key` (shown once, stored only as a hash) with **$27.50 of credit**, which is 27,500 cached
  verdicts or 27 batch screens. `pack1` is $1.00 for $1.10 of credit; `pack100` is $100.00 for $120.00
  (20 percent bonus). A `pack_test` tier at $0.02 exists for integration testing.
- Spend it with `X-Credit-Key: fxp_...`: `POST {"action":"redeem","route":"verdict","address":"0x...","chain":"base"}`
  or `route:"batch"` with up to 25 addresses. Credit is spent at list price and never expires.
- Check the balance free: `POST {"action":"balance"}` with the same header.
- Cached tiers only (verdict $0.001, batch $1.00). Live scan routes stay pay-per-call over x402,
  because each one spends real node reads.

## The cheap tier: $0.001 cached verdicts and $1.00 batch screens

Use these two when the job is screening rather than one-off checks. Both are answered from an hourly
precomputed feed, so they return in milliseconds instead of the 1 to 14 second live scan.

- `POST https://solene-fa2010da.base44.app/functions/verdictBatch` at **$1.00 per call**: up to 25
  token contracts in one request (`{"addresses":["0x...","0x..."]}`), each answer carrying grade,
  tier, score, roast and the full verdict object. That is $0.04 per token at the 25-token limit, and
  it is the route to use when an agent is screening a candidate list before committing capital.
  Tokens missing from the feed come back in `missed` with a pointer to the $0.02 live route; a batch
  with nothing cached is verified but never settled, so it costs nothing.
  Free coverage index for aiming a batch: `GET /functions/verdictFast?list=1`.
- First call from a new caller on the cached route is free, once per day, no parameter and no
  signup: `GET /functions/verdictFast?address=0x<token>&chain=base|ethereum` returns a real grade
  and roast at $0.00, then the paywall applies.

## The cheap tier: $0.001 cached verdicts

If you need a verdict in-path, on every trade, or thousands of times an hour, use the cached feed instead of the live scan:

- `GET https://solene-fa2010da.base44.app/functions/verdictFast?address=0x<token>&chain=base|ethereum` at **$0.001**
- Same letter grade A to F, roast, risk flags and next_calls as the $0.02 live verdict. Precomputed continuously in the background, answered from a key lookup instead of a 1 to 14 second chain scan.
- See exactly which tokens are in the feed for free: `?list=1` returns the whole cache with grades and timestamps.
- Coverage grows every ten minutes as the builder works through the token universe. If your token is not there yet, the call costs you nothing: the call returns `cache_miss: true` with a pointer to the live route, and no payment settles.

Use the cached route for volume and in-path decisions; use `/functions/forensicsApi?endpoint=verdict` ($0.02) when you need the current block.

## Try it free first

Add trial=1 to verdict, settlesafe, token, wallet or any single-question read for free daily calls per IP. No payment header needed, no signup. If a free call answers your question, stop there.

## See real responses before paying

Six verbatim responses captured from free trial calls, including the full grade range: USDC on Base grades A (RED_HOT), DEGEN grades D (THIN), BRETT grades F (SUSPICIOUS_THIN), plus a tokenized-equity settle screen, a wallet risk read and a mints micro read.

- Rendered with grades and roasts: https://onchainforensics.dev/samples.html
- Raw JSON, one file per call: https://onchainforensics.dev/openapi-samples/verdict-usdc-base.json, .../verdict-degen-base.json, .../verdict-brett-base.json, .../settlesafe-btsla.json, .../walletrisk-burn-base.json, .../mints-usdc-base.json

Nothing is mocked. If a sample answers your question, you already know what the paid call looks like.

## Why this is different

- Every payload states data_quality COMPLETE, PARTIAL or UNAVAILABLE. An unreadable chain is never reported as a zero, and an unattributable address is never reported as a guess.
- Reads come from a dedicated provider endpoint (Alchemy) that this service controls, with public gateways only as fallback, so a rate-limited shared node cannot turn a real balance into an empty read.
- No LLM in the decision path. Grades, tiers and roasts are deterministic functions of on-chain reads, so the same block gives the same answer.

## Routes and prices (all x402 v2, exact scheme, eip155:8453)

Base URLs:
- Gateway (directory + routing): https://solene-fa2010da.base44.app/functions/forensicsGateway
- Main API: https://solene-fa2010da.base44.app/functions/forensicsApi

Decision routes:
- info, FREE. Service card, endpoint catalog, pricing.
- verdict, $0.02. Token verdict card: verdict tier (RED_HOT/HEAVY_FIRE/ACTIVE/THIN/SUSPICIOUS_THIN/DORMANT...), activity score 0-100, transfers, unique wallets, mints/burns, concentration, flags, plain_take, letter grade, roast, next_calls.
- settlesafe, $0.02. Pre-trade trust screen for tokenized equities and RWAs: counterparty plus token screen (canonical registry, freeze and clawback flags), settle-risk verdict (KNOWN_CANONICAL and friends).
- trust, $0.02. One word back: TRUSTED, CAUTION, HIGH_RISK, UNVERIFIABLE or NOT_APPLICABLE, with reason codes and which checks actually ran.
- deployer, $0.05. Who launched the contract and from which wallet, plus deployer wallet age, tx count and an OFAC screen. On Base it returns LAUNCH_WINDOW_ONLY with a bracketed window and data_quality PARTIAL rather than guessing.
- token, $0.05. Full token profile: supply, holder concentration, top transfers, mint and burn history, whale moves.
- wallet, $0.05. Wallet trust screen: counterparty flows, contract interaction risk, trust tier.
- memo, $0.25 ($0.35 with counterparty screen). Composed due-diligence memo: multi-source verdict plus narrative risk assessment.
- canton, $0.05. Canton Network emission and burn-mint snapshot metrics.
- linea, $0.05. Linea burn-vault stats.

Single-question micro reads, $0.01 to $0.02: supply, activity, holders, contract owner, pause state, registry membership, 24h mints, 24h burns, wallet age, wallet funding origin, wallet flows, wallet risk.

Derivatives and equity issuance, $0.05: perp funding, open interest, option skew, tokenized-equity issuance.

All 33 routes with typed schemas: https://leohoudinisanders-byte.github.io/onchain-forensics/openapi.json

Chains: ERC-20s on Base and Ethereum (address plus chain params); Robinhood Chain including its 203 stock tokens; XRPL classic addresses (chain=xrp, issuer plus currency or a token alias); Solana SPL mints; Canton Network via verified entity snapshots.

Tokenized-equity and RWA aliases (19, all verified on-chain): btsla bcspx bcoin bnvda aapl nvda buidl usdy ousg ustb usyc ondo qnt xlm edel rlusd gatehub-usd bitstamp-usd bitstamp-eur.

## How to pay

Send any request, receive HTTP 402 with x402 v2 payment requirements (accepts[]), sign the EIP-3009 authorization with your wallet, retry with the X-PAYMENT header. Settlement on Base mainnet in USDC. Facilitator chain: CDP (Coinbase) primary, Roundhouse and PayAI fallback.

## MCP server (Claude, ChatGPT, any MCP client)

- Endpoint: https://solene-fa2010da.base44.app/functions/forensicsMcp (streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC 2.0)
- Tools: forensics_info (free), token_verdict ($0.02), settle_safe ($0.02), wallet_screen ($0.05), token_profile ($0.05), diligence_memo ($0.25 / $0.35 with counterparty)
- Same x402 pay-per-call: a paid tools/call returns HTTP 402 with PAYMENT-REQUIRED until paid, then sign and retry with X-PAYMENT.
- Also indexed in the Coinbase x402 Bazaar (type: mcp, transport: streamable-http).
